text:
Mira: quick thread — I think our current org-key vs project-token surface is too leaky for a lot of services. want to propose a smaller claim contract.
Jon: +1, can you sketch what "smaller" means?
Mira: basically two goals: 1) make runtime decisioning trivial (no expensive lookup to figure out intent), 2) keep least-privilege expressible without millions of token-types. tradeoffs below.
Sam: runtime perf is big — introspecting external DB per request is 🔥. prefer tokens with enough claims to avoid that.
Mira: proposal A: keep explicit token kinds (ORG_KEY, PROJECT_TOKEN) but standardize a tiny claimset: {kind, aud, proj_id?, intents[]}. proj_id optional for ORG_KEY if it was minted for admin use. runtime only checks kind+aud+intents.
Lee: sounds reasonable. what's the migration surface? a lot of apps minting org keys today.
Mira: migration plan idea: issue compatibility tokens with a bridging claim 'compat_scope' and a short TTL. auth proxy honours compat_scope for 90 days while owners move to project tokens.
Jon: alternative idea: proposal B = single-token model with an issuer-delegation chain encoded in claims: {iss_chain: [org, delegator], aud, scopes}. pros: fewer token classes, cons: makes token validation slightly more complex and increases token size.
Sam: B worries me because auditing gets harder — need to resolve iss_chain to human-readable owner. that implies extra lookup in console service.
Mira: agreed. A keeps runtime cheap at the cost of having two token kinds. B centralizes but adds ops cost.
Lee: for RBAC surface, I recommend we keep 'intent' as first-class claim (e.g., intents: [generate, embed, admin]) rather than mapping to role ids. makes per-request checks fast and stable.
Jon: +1 to intent. we can map intents to RBAC roles offline in the policy engine.
Mira: minimally viable claim examples (JWT payloads):
```
// ORG_KEY example
{
  "sub": "org:acme",
  "kind": "ORG_KEY",
  "aud": "redwood-api",
  "intents": ["admin:manage_pools"],
  "exp": 1758127056
}
// PROJECT_TOKEN example
{
  "sub": "proj:acme/payment",
  "kind": "PROJECT_TOKEN",
  "aud": "redwood-api",
  "proj_id": "acme/payment",
  "intents": ["inference:invoke"],
  "exp": 1758130656
}
```
Sam: that makes validation trivial. do we need a token-introspection endpoint for long-tail auditing?
Mira: yes — keep introspect for audit/console, not on the hot path. runtime should validate signature, aud, kind, and intents only.
Lee: telemetry: add a token-tag header we can pluck for metrics without parsing full claims to reduce CPU on hot path.
Jon: any objections to implementing A as the default and B as a follow-up design if we need consolidation later?
Sam: no objections. prefer A for predictable latency.
Mira: ok I'll draft a short RFC: "Compact token claims for fast runtime auth" with migration steps and sample SDK helpers. cc @auth-bot to create a tracking issue. :thumbsup:
auth-bot: created issue #9522 — RFC draft + migration checklist.
Mira: thanks — will post link when ready.
